market_name: Will 4 Fed rate cuts happen in 2026?

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether the market's implied cut count actually moved and whether Treasury futures (ZB/ZN) confirm a bull move; screen for any Fed speaker headlines or data surprise driving it.
time_plan.1h: Compare TLT and 10y/2y yield direction against the market signal; confirm move is not just noise or a spread compression.
time_plan.2h: Assess persistence — has TLT held the move or faded? Cross-check Fed funds futures (implied 2026 path).
time_plan.6h: Re-evaluate against any scheduled data/Fedspeak; decide if dovish repricing is broadening across curve and risk assets.
time_plan.12h: Mark final TLT return vs prediction; note whether the market probability shift preceded or lagged public rate repricing.

predictions.reasoning: A sharp rise in the implied probability of 4 Fed cuts in 2026 reflects a more dovish rate-path expectation. Lower expected policy rates pull down the yield curve, especially the long end, lifting long-duration bond prices. TLT is the most liquid, direct proxy for that expectation shift.

predictions.tradable_instrument_name: Invesco DB US Dollar Index Bullish Fund

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Verify DXY/UUP direction and whether the dollar move is Fed-driven vs a foreign-currency story.
time_plan.1h: Check EURUSD and rate-differential moves to confirm dovish USD channel.
time_plan.2h: Assess whether move persists or is offset by risk-off dollar demand.
time_plan.6h: Re-check against any ECB/BoJ headlines that could dominate FX.
time_plan.12h: Record UUP final return; note weak causal linkage and any confounds.

predictions.reasoning: More expected Fed cuts narrow US rate differentials, a headwind for the dollar. A dovish repricing typically weakens USD versus major peers, so UUP would drift lower. This is a weaker, second-order proxy because FX also reflects relative moves by other central banks.

evidence_used: Market question tracks the count of 25bps Fed cuts in 2026, a direct proxy for the expected policy-rate path
Standard macro linkage: dovish rate-path repricing lowers yields (bond prices up) and weakens the dollar
Liquid ETF/FX proxies (TLT, UUP) are the cleanest tradable expressions of Fed-path shifts
uncertainty_notes: 12h window is short; rate ETFs rarely move 700bps in half a day, so neither prediction meets the tradable threshold
A shift in a low-liquidity Polymarket probability may not reflect genuine new information about the Fed path
The topic tag 'military_conflict' appears mislabeled; this is a monetary-policy market
Long-end yields respond to term premium and inflation expectations, not just expected cuts, weakening the TLT link

llm_justification.summary: This is a monetary-policy prediction market on the number of 2026 Fed rate cuts. A sharp rise in the implied cut count signals a more dovish expected policy path, which maps to lower yields (higher long-bond prices, TLT up) and a modestly weaker dollar (UUP down). Both are directionally sensible but small in a 12h window and well below the 700bps tradable threshold, so this is low-confidence research signal rather than an actionable trade.
key_assumptions: The market probability actually moved sharply and reflects genuine rate-path repricing
Standard rate-transmission mechanics hold: fewer expected cuts priced = higher rates, and vice versa
No dominant competing driver (fiscal, risk-off, foreign central bank) overwhelms the Fed channel in the window
failure_modes: The dovish signal is already fully public (embedded in Fed funds futures), so proxies do not move on it
Long-end yields rise on term-premium/inflation concerns even as cut expectations grow, breaking the TLT link
Dollar strengthens on risk-off flows despite dovish Fed pricing, reversing the UUP call
Polymarket probability move is thin-liquidity noise with no informational content
Magnitude far below 700bps, so any apparent 'signal' is untradable and likely within noise
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
